assessment_metadata.title: Third-Party Vendor Cybersecurity Risk Assessment Template
assessment_metadata.assessor_notes: Quarterly third-party supplier cybersecurity maturity evaluation. Validating MFA, encryption keys, and incident SLA.

response_meanings.yes: Fully implemented and verified with documented audit evidence.
response_meanings.partial: Partially implemented or exceptions exist (e.g., SMS MFA instead of hardware tokens).
response_meanings.no: Control is missing or non-compliant (flags an identified security gap).
response_meanings.na: Not applicable to this vendor's scope of service.

answers.evidence: Audit check revealed that root and privileged administrator accounts do not enforce hardware/FIDO2 MFA.
answers.gap_notes: Privileged accounts exposed to credential stuffing and phishing attacks.

answers.evidence: RBAC matrix reviewed. Individual named accounts used for tenant management; quarterly access reviews verified.
TLS 1.3 enforced on all API endpoints; customer data encrypted using AES-256 with KMS key rotation.
Data retention policy mandates NIST SP 800-88 sanitization with cryptoshredding certificate upon contract termination.
Vendor agreement lacks a contractual 72-hour breach notification SLA; no record of tabletop exercises provided.
answers.gap_notes: Delayed incident notification could prevent timely mitigation during a supply chain compromise.

answers.evidence: Automated monthly vulnerability scans conducted, but critical CVE patch SLA currently averages 28 days instead of 14 days.
answers.gap_notes: Vulnerability exposure window is longer than acceptable enterprise risk threshold.

answers.evidence: Valid ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certificate and SOC 2 Type II report (dated within the last 9 months).
Automated daily geo-redundant backups with tested RTO of 4 hours and RPO of 15 minutes.
Vendor conducts annual risk reviews for Tier 1 hosting providers, but lacks a formal Software Bill of Materials (SBOM).
answers.gap_notes: Limited visibility into fourth-party open source library vulnerabilities.

answers.evidence: Mandatory background screening for all engineering personnel; bi-annual anti-phishing training simulated.
